utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karnavas, are you ready to continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Good morning. Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yesterday we left off on July 12th, 1995, when you indicated you had received an oral order, I believe it was the previous night, to go down in towards the area of Potocari. Now, do you recall giving a statement to the Prosecution back on 2nd December 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And have you had a chance to thoroughly read and review your statement?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, in your statement, and I'm making a reference to page 8. There are no lines in it. You seem to be indicating that you received that information on that morning -- on the morning of the 12th. And that's when you were told to move towards Potocari. So my question is: Were you mistaken when you gave the statement to the Prosecutor, or were you -- are you mistaken -- were you mistaken yesterday when you told us that it was the early evening that you received that order?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I received the order in the evening, and I was just made aware of my assignment in the morning, reminded of it. So both would be actually correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Now, could you please tell us what exactly you did on the 12th when you received that order. Where did you and your men go?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After a short preparation, the units which performed the assignment of Srebrenica, I followed them pursuant to orders, I started after them, which meant movement forward and advance and the clearing of the forest towards Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And how long -- or for how long I should say did you have to travel?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps one hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us what the terrain is like.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The terrain is forest terrain. It's a mountain terrain 4 to 500 metres altitude. It's a very steep terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is there a particular path that you were heading down to?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We were just moving through the forest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, as you were moving down the forest -- and I take it now you're heading into Potocari. Correct, in that direction?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: As you're moving through the forest, are you able to see Potocari?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I crossed to the other side, the other side of the hill, I wasn't able to see Potocari. However, we could see Gornji Potocari and the villages on the other hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. How about as you were moving down through the forest. Were you able to see Potocari?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, from halfway down the hill you could see Potocari, the other side of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When was the first time that you noticed that people had gathered at Potocari, at what point?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the very entrance to Potocari, which means as we emerged from the forest, you had the first houses, and that's where we encountered them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How close were they as you emerged from the forest?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At about 20 metres. As soon as you leave the forest, the houses start. And so that's where the people were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How many people did you see at that point?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, a lot of people, a whole village. People were there. There was a large quantity of people; I couldn't actually tell you how many. But there was so many people that it was difficult to move between them. That's the only way I can explain it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, according to your orders, how far were you supposed to go?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our order didn't not specify. We did have an order to move out and clear the forest until Potocari, but I didn't understand that to be stopping at the edge of the forest. I understood it to mean us to carry on. And it was inertia. You wanted to meet the people three years after the war. We simply had this desire to see the people, to meet them, at least the people we thought we knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. What was the reaction -- well, first of all, what was your reaction? Let's start there.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all suddenly as you left the forest and entered this mass of people, you thought that it might be the enemy. And this is a rather unpleasant feeling. So I was more collected perhaps than my soldiers. And some of the men panicked because they thought they had suddenly entered an ambush. Yes, it was a surprise; I was surprised, too. And the people were also surprised.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, did you notice any armed men when you got there, any armed Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you said some of your men panicked. Could you please describe how did they panic and what did they do, if anything?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't do anything, because mostly when my men were panicked, they would look to me for protection. So they stuck to me mostly. But then the panic dispersed because they saw they were ordinary people; it wasn't an ambush that we had fallen into. So that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you ever point your weapons, you and your men, did you ever point your weapons to that crowd of people?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. We had a different attitude. Well, we saw them. They were people -- they weren't the kind of people that you would have to cock your weapons at.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you ever order your men or see your men abuse any of the people in that crowd?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not then and not throughout the war. And my attitude was this: None of my soldiers could even have taken it into their head to abuse anyone, let alone to actually do it. And all the soldiers were actually looking for their friends, because most of them were from Srebrenica. So everybody had an acquaintance or friend and expected to come across one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, how many soldiers did you have with you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think about 58, because I had about 62 to begin with. But some of them stayed behind to stand guard over the equipment that was at the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And if I understand your previous answer, your men, in light of the location where you held that line, they came from Srebrenica, is that correct, most of them?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of them, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, how long did you stay in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That day, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one hour at the most.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what did you do during that one-hour period?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we went up on to the road leading through the village and then across the bridge to the asphalt Srebrenica/Bratunac road and reached the Distribucija building where the soldiers entered into the courtyard and we sat down to have a rest. And then a television crew turned up and asked me to make a statement. I gave the statement. We returned there. And afterwards General Mladic turned up and started making a noise saying we should advance forward. We stayed behind, because pursuant to orders it wasn't up to us to move forward. But we hid from him, we hid in front of him so he couldn't see us. And then some 15 to 20 minutes later, I received an order from the battalion command. I think it was a courier that brought the order telling me to go back to the lines, the Potocari/Peciste/Djogazi line, which is what I actually did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to go through that answer a little bit in more detail, step by step. How long had you been in Potocari before General Mladic showed up?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not even 10 minutes. He was round about there somewhere, but that's when we actually saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How close were you to General Mladic when he showed up?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps 10 metres. Because the general is that kind of man, and I even saw colonels fleeing from him or trying to dodge him and not actually have to face him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And do you -- did you recognise any other generals that were with General Mladic at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you recognise or did you see, I should say, your own commander of the Bratunac Brigade there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't see anybody from our brigade. And as to the people from the corps, or wherever they were from, I never ever met them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, when General Mladic started yelling, telling the soldiers to advance, what did you take that to mean? Did he give you concretely a location where to go?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he said: "Forward, forward to Milacevici, Gornji Potocari, Milacevici." That general direction. That's what he had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, did he say this personally to you, or was he just... ?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he said it to everyone, all of us there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And did you start moving in that direction?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We just moved behind the building, moved out of his sight. Because for me, the order I was to listen to was the order given to my battalion -- from my battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the only order I was supposed to listen to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And how much longer after that did you receive the message from the courier for you to move your position?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe 10 to 15 minutes later. But it's difficult to set a time, because time flies. But 10 to 15 minutes I would say, not longer than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is it possible that your commander came looking for you and gave you the order himself, the commander of the battalion?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think he did. And in my statement from Banja Luka -- I'm not quite sure, actually. There is some mention of me saying Zoran -- well, the order was issued by him, so perhaps there was a mistake there. But it was handed to me by a courier. I didn't see Zoran there at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, during that entire period that you were there, what did you and your men actually do with respect to the crowd of people, if anything?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything we did, that is to say the soldiers did this individually. They tried to find a friend or acquaintance, come into contact with someone they knew, that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were you carrying any weapons at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, when you got this order, where were you to move? What was your next -- the next location that you were to go to?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next location was Potocari, Pecista, Djogazi. From the line, I had come down the hill into that mass of people. That's where my line stretched, left towards Bratunac, at the foot of the mountain itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When you left Potocari, do you know whether General Mladic was still there, or had he moved on?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you were interviewed in Banja Luka, did you have an opportunity to look at a map and assist the Office of the Prosecution in locating your positions?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On that map, we drew in, or rather, I drew in the positions of my unit before we moved towards Potocari and the unit's positions where I went after Potocari. So the map was I think marked A, B, and D, or something like that. And I drew in the road which we took when we withdrew to Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, perhaps you could assist us. If you could look at a copy of the section of the map that we received from the Office of the Prosecution. And if need be, we can show you the original one if you can't make it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I guess we need to give this an identification number. I believe it would be 135.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Or it could be 142. D142/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Can you see the map on the monitor?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, it's next to you on this little projector. So if you need to point to it, you'll have to turn and actually point on the map itself. Okay. So we'll take it slowly. If you could please tell us -- first of all, do you recognise the markings on this map?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Whose markings are they?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mine, my markings. I put the D and the E and the C letters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if you could explain what all these markings mean, I would appreciate it. And let's start with -- first, could you please tell us where your line was located, where your company was located.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before we set out --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This C here is the line of Obadi, and that was the position I was at before I set out for Potocari. And D --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: One step at a time. One step at a time. That line, could you please -- where it says "C" on the exhibit, how far did it extend? How far did your company extend? What was the line of defence that you were holding?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The line of defence was from Caus hill above Potocari on the other side. So the peak was held by the other unit. And on the other slope was where my line began and it went through Obadi, where I had unit headquarters, and then it went towards Zalazje. And the length of the line was about 3 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Can you show us that on the map itself, where your line was. All right from there --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's it here. You go Obadi. That is the HQ. And then towards Zalazje -- actually, that's where Caus is. Obadi/Zalazje is this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now -- for the record, you pointed to where the C is located, that particular line. Could you please tell us for how long were you at that position prior to July 12th, 1995.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at that position from March 1993 to the end, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you move from that line from July 6 to July 11, 1995?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We stayed at that line until the 12th, and we didn't return.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if you could show us from there, where did you traverse on the 12th.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 12th, I set out from Obadi, from the elevation, Caus elevation or feature, and I went slowly down the hill. And I reached the edge -- the outskirts of Pecista, because there were people from Pecista already. So that's the line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And the record should reflect that you're pointing from the northern or the uppermost part of the line with the C, and it's heading towards, I believe, the D. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, for those of us who are not that familiar with maps, these little ridges, what does that mean? From C -- or the area that you travelled, you see all these little lines, what does that designate? Does that designate the terrain?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the configuration of the terrain. It's a slope towards Potocari, and from that main slope you have different hills branching off. So that is the configuration of the terrain; that's what it's like. Because as I said it's at an altitude of 4 to 500 metres, and you go up this -- up above sea level in minutes; it's steep.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, if we go to the line where you have the D, before we talk about that line, if we keep going leftwards, we see a couple of lines. Is that the road that goes from Bratunac to Potocari and on to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the road goes this way, that that's the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Okay. So that would be the road. Where would Srebrenica be, in which direction?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This direction, down here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. We can't see --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is west of Bratunac and the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, could you please tell us from the location D to the road, what is the distance?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the location, my unit's location to the road is in a straight line, as the crow flies, about 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, as I understand it, right around that area, there's an industrial park.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. That's the whole compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Where would that be? Could you point it out, please.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between, say, Pecista, Djogazi. That's that factory park and compound moving up to Potocari. This industrial park begins from the left-hand side of the road from Bratunac to Srebrenica, and then it moves on to the right-hand side of the road. That entire area and compound is an industrial zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's look at what you've marked as A, D, and E. Could you please explain to us what these -- what this line means or lines.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The D line means my unit's position after its return from Potocari. The E line is the line I set out from, from Potocari, on my way to Borici, the command of the battalion, from whence I went on to Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So just to make sure I understand it. When you went down to Potocari, down the hill, the location where you and your men stayed at was right around that line designated D. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And the line from E to A, E is where you set off after you received the orders in Potocari and you headed off to the location of A. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now -- and you see the A is circled right around the road itself, the asphalt road. If you head north, we would go towards Bratunac, would we not?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, could you please tell us, if you -- if it's possible, where is the Zuti Most, the yellow bridge? Can we see it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's this here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You have to point on the projector.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So from A going north towards Bratunac, what would the distance be?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About a kilometre and a half, 100 or 20 metres, plus or minus, because this is where I live and I often use that bridge. I think it's 1.000 or 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, where were the battalion command headquarters located?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The battalion headquarters was in Borici, marked A and circled. Here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So basically, if I understand you correctly, you were told on that day to head back and hover around with your men at the battalion headquarters?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That wasn't the order I received. My order was to collect the soldiers and come to the battalion command, and that there would be buses waiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But is this on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Well, I want to be clear now. Where were you told on the 12th of July to go to?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 12th of July, as far as I can recall, that's the day I was in Potocari when I went back to the position marked D. And I stayed there. There were no other orders or tasks. The first task I received after that was to report to the battalion headquarters, and there I was told to proceed to Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, I need to clarify that, because I might have confused everybody here, including myself. On the 12th, after you got to Potocari and you mingled with the men, are you now stating that you went back from Potocari some distance to where the D is located?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, leading. I think it would be a lot clearer if the witness did the testifying.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm trying to clarify a point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe you could go step by step.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll go step by step.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Please designate to us exactly where you went once you received the order on the 12th of July while you were in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went back along the same way I had taken to arrive in Potocari, that is, I went on to the road for 200 or 300 metres in the direction of Srebrenica. I passed to the left side of the river and took the village lane to Potocari. And that is the end of Potocari or the beginning of Peciste. There is a village road that goes Potocari, Peciste, Djogazi. And that was my line where I remained with my unit. Those were the last inhabited houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please show us where on the map that is located.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. I think this village road should be there, passing from the road through here, arriving to Peciste. At Peciste at the foot of the mountain, and then going on towards Djogazi. I think this is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Where did you end up?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And finally, I arrived at this village road marked D. That's the Djogazi/Peciste/Potocari village road, where my line was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So on the 12th you stayed where it's designated D?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How long were you in that location?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't assert with precision, but I do know I remained there until I set out for Zvornik. In Banja Luka, we tried to put the dates together, but dates never meant much to me. We agreed there that the 12th, Petrovdan was the day we were in Potocari. We stayed there until we set out for Zvornik, which would have been on the 15th at 10.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, where were you when you set off to go to Zvornik, what location?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at the location marked D.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And where did the buses pick you up?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of the headquarters of the battalion in Borici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When you went to the headquarters over there of the battalion, were you aware what your assignment was going to be?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When you got there, who gave you your assignment?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I got there, my battalion commander from the battalion command, that's where I got the task, we were told to go to Zvornik to secure the Zvornik/Tuzla road. That's at Crni Vrh. That's what we were told.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How many men did you have with you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 58.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, it's the Prosecution's theory that members of the Bratunac Brigade, perhaps your unit, went in that direction in order to commit atrocities. Did you and your men stop anywhere on the way on that day or the next day or any other day, and commit the atrocities that the Prosecution believes the Bratunac Brigade was engaged in?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection to him stating what he thinks our case is, because he hasn't got it right yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I have been listening to those intercepts yesterday, Your Honour. I thought I was getting a clue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Those were members of the Visegrad brigade that checked in to the Bratunac Brigade before they went up there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you may put your question another way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were you ever given any orders to commit any atrocities?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Our orders were very strict. The buses took us to Zvornik; that was their task. I was to report to the chief of the brigade, Mr. Obrenovic, down there. And we didn't hang around. There was no need to stop along the way. As for the story going around, I heard about that only after making that statement in Banja Luka, that is, that our unit was mentioned as one of the units that possibly did this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, what time did you arrive in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, between 12.00 and 12.30. Let's say around 12.00 noon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And did you -- who did you see when you arrived in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I don't know anyone in Zvornik, in front of the headquarters there were already some people waiting for me. I was taken into Mr. Obrenovic's office. There was another man there, probably the leader of a unit, and he gave both of us the same information, that is, that there was certain enemy forces there. And he said that he assumed there were three groups, two groups of about 2.000 men, or rather, women and elderly, whom we should not pay attention to because they were not a threat to Zvornik. And there was another group where they were all extremists. He mentioned the name of Zulfo Tursum, a man whom we on our territory considered to be a man who burnt down of our villages. We said that this group had the task of breaking through to Tuzla or dying in the attempt. And our task was to strengthen the defence lines there and if possible to make the group go back to the old Zvornik/Tuzla road in order to break it up as far as was possible. That was our task and we were given a guide and told to report to the command of the 4th Battalion at Baljkovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Let me take it again step by step. First of all, how many buses of soldiers went to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had only one bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So all your men were in one bus?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you know Mr. Obrenovic from before?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, and I probably wouldn't recognise him today. That was our only encounter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you know Major Jokic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not from the Zvornik -- from the Zvornik Brigade, I only knew Mr. Pandurevic, I knew him through sight, not through personal contacts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What was Obrenovic's demeanor as he was describing to you the events that were unfolding on the front lines?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was normal. There was no panic, no hysteria. He explained the situation to us and gave us our tasks in a very normal manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did he show you a map of where you would be going?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't show us the map. He gave us a guide who took us there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did he explain to you what the terrain looked like?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was the task given to the battalion commander up there where we reported.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But I'm asking you: Before heading off to this mission, were you explained by Obrenovic what the terrain looked like?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you have a map with you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Had you been in that area before during the period when you had been mobilised?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, neither before nor after. And I wouldn't know the way there today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you indicated that Mr. Obrenovic told you that you would be going off to the 4th Battalion and that a guy would be taking you there. Did that happen?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, please explain to us where the 4th Battalion was located, what you saw, what you learned, what you did.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I arrived at that hill, I don't know what it's called, the buses went back. My men sat down to have a rest. And I went with the commander of the 4th Battalion to tour his lines, which were to be strengthened during the night. And when we had made the tour and returned after a certain time, we had a rest. And then we received an order to the effect that we were not to remain there, although it was starting to get dark, but that rather we should go to the river valley down to Baljkovica itself. And we were told that our unit would be given its task when it arrived there. From there, there was a military truck that we got on to. And there was a slope. We were going downhill, and we were observed by the Muslim forces right away. The mortar and machine-guns started firing at us. The truck was moving along as fast as we could, and we jumped out of the truck with our equipment and took cover, running down the hill toward the stream. The truck made several trips, and that's how we made our way along the stream, through the woods, and arrived at where the 5th Battalion was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received a task from the 5th Battalion, from the commander of that battalion or his deputy. I can't say which. And he -- from the battalion command, we went for about -- their men were deployed for about 100 or 150 metres. And then I was to be their left flank, covering the area going on from there. And they said that our left flank would be units from Sekovici, but unfortunately in the morning I saw that this was not true because we were there on our own. And we stayed there the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Incidentally, did you lose any men? Did you have any casualties?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When we were getting out of the truck to go toward the 5th Battalion, one of my men who wore 37-size boots, but he had 42-size shoes on. And he lost his shoes in the swamp we were moving through, so he was barefoot. And I left him in the battalion command, because he couldn't go with us barefoot. In the morning when there was an attack, he went missing. But fortunately three days later, he joined the unit at Crni Vrh. He managed to flee and rejoin the unit later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But you didn't lose any men? Nobody lost their life? They lost their boots, lost their way, but they didn't lose their life?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't. Fortunately, that's how it was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, during that period did you return any fire against the Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Throughout the night, there was artillery fire. At first we thought it was ours, but then during the evening, the Muslim forces took a mortar battery, I think it was. And I received the news by courier in the night from the Zvornik Brigade that at around 10.00 p.m. the Muslim forces had taken some of our artillery. And they fired it. We thought it was our own artillery, but it was they who were using it. And they fired, as it turned out, on an empty area where there were no men. They were clearing the space for the following day. During the night, it rained; there was ice. We didn't return fire. There was no fighting. It was only artillery fire, and an occasional shot or two. At daybreak, maybe before 5.00 a.m., the attack began, as I thought, and it was close by. The attack went along the river, which means that the focus was on the 5th Battalion command. There was fighting close to where I was, but it passed us by, and we didn't have any firing on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, how long did you stay in that location?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed there until perhaps 10.00, because those forces were already behind my back. They had broken through the line, so I was cut off. And I went more to the left with my unit as I thought in the direction of Snagovo or Crni Vrh. And that's where I managed to get to Crni Vrh and then on to the Tuzla road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And then from there where did you go?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think -- we didn't have time to think. We didn't look at our watches or think about the time, but I think it was at around 10.00 that we started to pull out. At first there were five or six men with radio equipment, and they tried to contact their command. But the voices that responded were not familiar, and artillery fire followed us constantly. So we agreed, the communications man and I, to give us these attempts to communicate, because we saw that the artillery was following us because of our radio equipment. They went with us for a while, and then they lagged behind. What happened to them further, I don't know. We didn't have any maps or compasses, so we continued moving through this unfamiliar terrain. But knowing the Zvornik/Tuzla road, my intention was to get out on to this road. I went more to the left than I wanted to. I thought I would get out to the right of Snagovo, but I actually came out on the road 3 or 4 kilometres away from Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Had you been given orders to move in any direction?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. From Baljkovica, I pulled out on my own initiative, because it was not possible to receive any orders. Our radio communications were cut off. I was unable to contact my brigade command. And secondly, I had been attached to the Zvornik Brigade. So I was forced to make a decision on my own, either to stay there, which would not have been a good thing, or to pull out, which I did. And fortunately, I saved my own life and the lives of my men in this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Perhaps to save some time, it was part of the Prosecution's case that these gents got lost. And so this is not a contested issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I know it's hard to remember of all of this, but if we go back to some of the other testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am fully aware of the Prosecution's case, irrespective of their earlier comments. But I think each witness is entitled to tell their story in a sequential order, because we're getting there. So I appreciate the kind concession by the Prosecutor, but we were about to move on to the next segment of where we went from there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, in some parts, maybe we could move a little bit faster.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I agree with you, Your Honour, but as we know with some of the witnesses wish to be as thorough as they can, but I will, I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: From that road, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I got on to the Tuzla/Zvornik road, I came across some forward command post probably, where Major Zoran Jovanovic was. Major Jovanovic, not the Zoran Jovanovic from our battalion. I reported to him, told him what happened, and then he sent us to a school which was about a kilometre or a kilometre and a half away. We stayed there and rested until the early evening, and in the evening somebody came from the Zvornik Brigade with a bus and took us back to the Zvornik/Tuzla road. And from the quarry to Tuzla, that's where I deployed my men. And it was only then that we started securing the Zvornik/Tuzla communication in the Crni Vrh area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, the Major Zivanovic [sic], from which brigade is he from?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you were moved to the new location, the Zvornik/Tuzla -- to secure the Zvornik/Tuzla communication, how long were you there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the evening of the 16th and the evening of the 17th, two evenings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And did anything happen during those two evening?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing happened during the night. In daytime we looked at the Muslims across the meadows, going in groups, one by one, or in groups of ten. That's what I saw in the morning. But at night, they would come to the road. They could creep up to the road, cross the road, and go on toward Tuzla. Our instructions were to let larger groups through and to send smaller groups back. There was never any other order. And one morning, I think it was on the 16th in the evening or the 17th in the morning, they woke me up and they said they were crossing. And we counted them. They were 30 men who would cross over, crouch by the road, and then they would pass through the houses between us and go on. And we let them through. We watched them, but we let them through, because that was what had been agreed on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So you didn't engage them at all?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was not my task.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And incidentally, on page 24, line 1, it states Major Zivanovic. It's not Major Zivanovic, but Major Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jovanovic, Jovanovic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, when did you return to the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, or rather, I'm sure, because I stayed there two nights, that on the 18th buses arrived to pick me up. Let me mention that on the 17th another unit arrived and spent the night with us. They were from Bratunac. So two buses came on the 18th and we went back together.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, that unit that showed up on the 17th, do you know who was the commander or the komandir of that unit?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was Predrag Ilic, and it was the 3rd Company from my battalion, and he told me that already on the evening of the 16th, they arrived at the Zvornik Brigade late and that they stayed in the barracks, spent the night there, so that on the 17th they would come up to the line and stay just that one night.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did Mr. Ilic tell you that he had been given any orders to link up with Lukic or anyone else to commit any atrocities in the Zvornik area?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did any of his men or he himself tell you that they had been engaged in committing atrocities in Branjevo Farm or Pilica or anywhere else in that area?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. May I be allowed to add something very briefly? Our brigade and our men were men who were at -- up at the front lines all the time. So you couldn't find anybody for that assignment. And it would be illusory to look for that. Other units, independent units, did that. And as for this particular unit, the one coming from 3rd Company, I think that they had problems in Bratunac because people refused to come, so that's why they had to stay late. So to expect something from people like that was illusory and everybody was aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, once you got to Bratunac, what was your next assignment?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we got to Bratunac, to the battalion, we were told that -- I was told that I was to let the men go that day, but that we should muster again the next day at 10.00 in front of the battalion, and that we were to going advance to Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And did you go off to Zepa?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the next day, at 10.00. We set out by bus towards Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Incidentally, getting back, just to clarify one point. Your line, your permanent line, of your company prior to July 12, 1995, did it face-off or was it in front of any Muslim forces, the 28th Division that was in this demilitarised enclave?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In front of me were two UNPROFOR points, the DutchBat. There weren't even any villages in between, because there was one hill called Zanik and underneath that was UNPROFOR. On the left-hand side, that same hill, on the right-hand side right below me. So no, there were no units, or villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: One moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, very much, sir. I believe Mr. Stojanovic may have a question or two, then Mr. McCloskey, the Prosecutor, and the Judges. So I would appreciate it if you would be as frank and forthright with them as you have been with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic, do you have any questions to this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Good morning, Witness. Just a few questions, Your Honours, with respect to the events on the 15th in the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kovacevic, during the examination-in-chief today you said you did not know Dragan Jokic. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, the -- my follow-up question, the man who is here and you see as Dragan Jokic, did you see that man at the command of the Zvornik Brigade at all?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think only Mr. Obrenovic was in the office there, that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You have described what Mr. Obrenovic looked like and what he told you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said what he told me. Now, if I saw him in the courtroom here, I don't think I'd recognise him.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you gain the impression that he was a well-informed individual about the situation up at the front and on the battlefield, and that he was kept abreast of the military operations within the area of responsibility of his brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the impression I gained, but when I returned I met, or rather, I bypassed a group, about 3.000 men. The group he said that we shouldn't take account of much. So I think he was well-informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So as we say he was in charge of the situation, knowing the position of his own units and the enemy units as well. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that he wasn't prone to panic, that he was a calm person, do you conclude by that that he was stable in the brigade command, that is to say that he was well aware of the situation at brigade headquarters and in the area of responsibility of his unit. Is that what you meant?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was what I meant. That was the impression he gave.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So you would say that all of this went on at around 12.00, would you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because at 10.00 -- yes, exactly 12.00, give or take 10 minutes. Maybe a little after 12.00, but I don't think it was much before 12.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And you didn't see -- or did you see any police officers, policemen or police officers, anybody from the police?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see anybody then.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, the thesis of this Defence case is that on the -- in the morning of the 15th, Mr. Beara was not at the command of the Zvornik Brigade. Now, our question in that respect is: Do you know Mr. Beara?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw Mr. Beara at our brigade during the war, and I do believe that at the time I would have recognised him. But I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So in those afternoon hours, you did not see him at the command or the headquarters of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was only Obrenovic who was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you this for a very simple reason, because I understood it from the examination-in-chief that in addition to Obrenovic there was another man there who you didn't know and who didn't join in the conversation.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, that was a man who was probably the komandir of a unit. Because Obrenovic spoke and issued assignments that I gained the impression that that was also a man from some other unit on the same side as me, not the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's why I'm asking you. So that man, you would have recognised it if he were --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And you assumed that he was from the Zvornik Brigade, did you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, quite simply, I thought it was somebody from the Zvornik Brigade, the komandir of one of the units of the Zvornik Brigade, perhaps. But as I say, he didn't get involved in the conversation; he just listened, just like I did. And I think he left the premises together with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. My suggestion is that we have an early break, and we'll resume at 20 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey. Your cross-examination, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And good morning, everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir, when you were in Zvornik in the headquarters, you couldn't possibly have seen all the different officers that were in the headquarters building that day, could you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not talking about the headquarters; I'm talking about Mr. Obrenovic's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's the only office you went in in that building. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't know the building. They took me into that room, or rather, into the building. Now, what there is in the building, I can't say. I can assume that there wasn't only that office.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I asked you if that was the only office you went in. Did you go in some other office, besides Obrenovic's?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, just that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So you didn't go into the security office or the duty office or the commander, Pandurevic's, office?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Or the coffee room where they have a big table and coffee?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. You also told us something that I think there's some support for, that regular soldiers, the line soldiers, the conscripts are not the most well-disciplined group in the world and probably not anyone's first choice as an execution squad. Is that basically what you were saying?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I wanted to say is: The people who guarded the defence in our brigade and probably in Zvornik were not people who could go into action; they just weren't. That is something that only the independent units could have done who did not -- were not responsible to anyone. They worked for themselves mostly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So when you say "go into action," what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I mean to attack; that's what I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So you're not talking about war crimes? You're talking about attack units?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, those attack units, you have units there which are well-disciplined soldiers, young men who are ready to carry out orders in an attack. No, I'm talking about the other units which are prone, to my mind, and anything dirty they did, anything of that kind, was done by some independent units, because as I see it -- well, this is not a nice thing to say, but they are clochards, if I can put it that way. That's the only word I can find to describe people like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, well we're not talking about 1992 when some rather bad folks were in paramilitary units and doing things; we're talking about July 1995. Now -- and just talking about attack units, disciplined attack units, that can go into a disciplined attack. Would the Red Berets of the Bratunac unit be a disciplined attack unit?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, the Green Berets is the Muslim side, and we didn't collaborate with them. As to the Red Berets, we had one unit of that kind, and to my mind that was a highly responsible unit, a unit which deserved, or rather, helped Bratunac survive. So a unit like that wouldn't have done anything like that. And secondly, that unit wasn't in Bratunac at that time within the composition of our brigade, because they had left, they had gone on. I think they were in Dalj or some such place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: They were given a job around Milici around the 12th or 13th of July, according to the records we have. Does that refresh your recollection on where the Red Berets were?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't refresh my recollections. I don't know. I can't say yes or no. Quite simply, I do not know. I am not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know a Red Beret, I think his name is Milenko Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name doesn't ring a bell. I don't know. Milenko Stojanovic. The surname might be from Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour. But the surname Stojanovic has been recorded and the first name is Milenko. Now, is it Stojanovic or Stanojevic, I think? Let's clear that up, and then we can clear the interpretation up. And I don't want the witness to be placed in this unfortunate situation of having to answer to the wrong name. I apologise for having to intervene.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Stojanovic. I -- Mr. Stojanovic is right and I'm sorry, I've gotten my names slightly mixed up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The name -- can you tell us the name that Stanojevic, Miroslav Stanojevic, sorry about my name.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So now the first name and the last name seems to be different. Miroslav Stanojevic you're asking me about now. No, that doesn't ring a bell either. Perhaps I know the man by sight, but the name doesn't mean anything to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: He died in an automobile accident a couple of years ago I think around Bratunac somewhere.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did the Red Berets, were they commanded by the brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Red Berets, to my mind, while they existed and were in Bratunac, were under the command of our brigade. And I think they were well-disciplined men and the right type of unit, if I can put it that way, to go into operations and carry out assignments. But I'm not sure that that whole unit was complete because -- now, if you say the whole unit was there, but I thought, or rather, I thought that that whole unit had been sent to Dalj three or four months earlier, that it had left the Bratunac Brigade, as far as I remember. I might be wrong, but that's what I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the Bratunac Brigade had a military police platoon as well, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Were those military police officers better disciplined than your average conscript soldier?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you know that two military police officers were at the Pilica school on the 16th and 17th of July when over 1.000 Muslims were murdered in and around the Branjevo Farm near that school?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may just --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may register a minor objection. There is a note in a logbook that they were there; it hasn't been established that they were in fact there. So I think there's a big distinction, especially since we know that record-keeping during that period of time was far from perfect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, this objection is registered in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: There's also evidence beyond that logbook, which I won't get into now, but there is evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So you never heard about that. You said you heard some stories about Bratunac being in that area, but that's not one of -- you never heard a thing about those MPs being at the Pilica school?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you hear the story that a busload of Muslims, as they came out of the bus at the Pilica school, were shot and murdered with automatic weapons?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's leave Zvornik for now and go back to before the enclave fell. I think you or someone else said that -- well, let me ask you: Were any soldiers from your company or your battalion loaned down to the 3rd Battalion at any time in the weeks before the enclave was attacked, and the enclave was attacked on 6th July?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our brigade held a position first of all somewhere up there from Han Pijesak, Stijanski [phoen] hill, and then we took over a part of the responsibility of holding the line at Trnovo, Treskavica, that is to say above Sarajevo. So we always sent a certain number of men there and they were replaced from time to time. Now, four to five days before at Srebrenica, upon assignment from the battalion, I appointed four men. I was supposed to give five. One was from Praha [phoen] and disappeared in Bratunac and he was in hiding. I didn't know about that until the fall of Srebrenica and my return from Zvornik. I thought he was there, whereas the man said he hid and didn't come out of his hiding place for some time. So those are all the men that we gave.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It was a simple question. I asked you if you sent any of your men on loan to the 3rd Battalion, not to Trnovo. Did you send any of your men to help out the 3rd Battalion in the days before the attack?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've just answered, sir. Four days before that, I sent four men to help out the 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And in June did you send anybody down to help out the 3rd Battalion for the attack on OP Echo near Zeleni Jadar?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Were you aware of the VRS attack on OP Echo in June, this Dutch observation post at Zeleni Jadar that was right at the approach towards Srebrenica from the south?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know about that. I just had contacts with the battalion, and even when I went home I didn't hear about that. And usually all the things I did learn about were round town, as we say, going about the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Did the 2nd Battalion have any heavy mortars or any mortars at all?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 2nd Battalion had a mortar battery of 82-millimetre calibre, as far as I know. And it served the needs of the entire battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how close was that battery -- what elevation or location was that mortar battery located on in July 1 of 1995?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where it was located I don't know, but as far as I know they didn't change their positions throughout. At the beginning of the war, they were sent to that location, and they stayed there until the end of the war. And I think that was from the rear of the brigade command, at the outskirts of town. They weren't up at the elevation, but behind the hill, or rather at the foot of the hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did your battalion have any artillery?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The whole artillery just had that mortar battery, as far as I know. I think at an elevation there was a ZIS weapon, a ZIS. First of all, there was a recoilless gun which exploded and there was some dead, casualties, on our side. And after that, just one ZIS, I believe, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you tell us what a ZIS is.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, I think it's a 120-millimetre cannon, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And where was it located in early July?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was located behind the lines of the 2nd Company of my battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did it fire at all on the early days of July leading up to the attack and the attack on Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't say. I can't say yes or no. I just don't know. I think -- I do not think it fired. I don't remember hearing any gunfire or explosions, which of course does not exclude the possibility. So I can't say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And you've told us that on the 12th that both on the night of the 11th and the morning of the 12th, you got orders to go down towards Potocari. Right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And that you went down through the woods and you went into the Potocari area amongst the crowd of Muslims. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you think you were violating your orders by going in amongst the crowd?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order was not very clear on this. It was quite vague. So most probably I did overstep the limits of my task, but the instructions were not complete. Had they been, they would have mentioned the line I was to stay at. The instructions or the order was imprecise in this respect, so I may have erred. If it's anyone's fault, it's mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And you told us that you and your men were interested in seeing the Muslims, to greet old friends, meet and greet old friends. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is that your testimony today?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why not? That's the kind of people we are. One day we fight and the next day we live together normally. We've been warring for centuries. It's nothing to us. A friend is a friend. But when we have rifles in our hands, that's different, but we're not angry at each other. I have members of my family who have been killed, my brother among them, but I'm not angry. That was the way things were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, there was a lot of members of your battalion that had friends and family killed by the enemy, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have over 20 members of my family who were killed, my extended family and also my closer family.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And many of those men might not be so good-hearted as you and might actually carry a grudge, wouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my unit, there was hardly anyone who had not had people killed in their families. But everybody wanted this to be over. They all wanted to go home. They all understood that the other side was in the same situation we were in, so no, we did not have grudges. We were angry at our leaders more than anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You can speak for all your 58 soldiers; there wasn't an angry one among them?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I guarantee that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Wasn't it a commander's duty to know that his troops might get out of hand when faced with the enemy or the family of the enemy?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that, but I also know that I had authority over my men. They respected me and they didn't dare do anything that I did not allow them to. That's why I can guarantee for every one of my men then, and at any other time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, that's very honourable that you speak to highly of your men, but you're sure you can get into each one of their hearts and minds and tell us whether or not they were angry? You're sure about that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were with me for three years. I know them well. I know how they tick. I know whether they had any problems. They were like family to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you see any military-age Muslims in the crowd you were amongst for that hour period that you spoke of?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How many, roughly?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a huge crowd of people, men, women, and children, all in civilian clothes, ranging in age from 2 to 70 or 80. It was a mixed crowd, but none of them were in uniform -- or at least I didn't see anyone in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But they could have been hiding weapons under their shirt or in their pants, couldn't they?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but in the woods we found lots and lots of weapons, especially on the way back from Zvornik. We didn't find any soldiers, but we found lots of weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you report that to your superiors or to anyone that they were able-bodied Muslim men amongst the crowd where you were?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Nobody asked me about that. It wasn't my task.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Was there any buses or trucks there in Potocari amongst the crowd when you were there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the road as far as I was able to see, but I didn't look to see how many or what kind of buses or trucks they were, what was written on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you see other people in camouflage uniforms, aside from your own soldiers, in the crowd and around the crowd?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were only our units there. I saw I think it was some sort of police unit going towards Milacevici where the general said they should go. I think they were in uniforms that were either black or dark blue, navy blue. I can't be sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: When you say "there were only our units there," are you talking about other Bratunac Brigade units than your company?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm referring to the Army of Republika Srpska. They were not from our brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So there were other units from the Army of Republika Srpska in Potocari when you were?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Roughly how many did you see?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's hard to say among that crowd. It may have been 50 or 100. This unit I mentioned I think was between 30 and 50 men. They were going on towards Gornji Potocari. I think between 30 and 50 men, but they kept moving around.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you see Muslim men of military age, able-bodied men, separated from their families in Potocari that day?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We were at the entrance to Potocari or in front of this factory where they gathered together. And all the people were there. I didn't see that being done. People were milling around.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you see any Muslims get hit or kicked or shot?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm certain no one was hit. Throughout this time that I was there, I never heard any shots, and I believe that nobody fired any shots, because there was no fighting going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, there was many dead bodies in Potocari on those days from Muslim men. The Court has seen photographs of some of them, we've heard about the Serb sanitation people that picked up several, we've heard from witnesses that have testified about bodies around Potocari. You never -- you have no idea how those people died?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have no idea. I don't know. I didn't hear about that. I wasn't interested, and I didn't want to see or know things I wasn't interested in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Isn't it your duty to be interested in protecting soldiers, be they prisoners of war or civilians?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had I taken them prisoner and had they been in my care, they certainly would have been protected. These were others and we could do nothing about that. I probably made a mistake in going down there. Someone might hold it against me, but it happened. As for what you say, during this time while I was there and on my way back, I did not see any dead people. I just saw women, children standing by the roadside, sitting down. I'm sure I didn't see anyone killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If you saw other soldiers abusing a civilian in front of you, beating them, would you feel it your duty to do anything about that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would it have been my duty? It's everybody's duty to protect them, so it would have been my duty, too. But the units working on that terrain were superior to us. I did not have the right, nor would it ever occur to me to interfere with what they were doing. However, had I seen something like, I couldn't have kept quiet. I don't know what I would have done. It is not wise to oppose units like those.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If an officer is present, a senior officer is present, at a scene where people are abused openly and that officer does nothing to stop that, what, if anything, is he communicating to his troops who are there and who see this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I were with a unit and if I had done this, that would have been a signal to my soldiers that they can do that, too. But no honourable officer would allow that. Most of our officers were honourable men. There were both kinds in this war. That's how it was. I would not have allowed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. So if you're present and civilians are being abused and you do nothing about it in front of your troops, that would be a signal to your troops that it was okay. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my view, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, that signal to your troops that it's okay to beat somebody, that would be encouraging those troops to beat people, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So by the very fact of a commander knowing that there's abuse going on, when he communicates that lack of any conduct to his troops, that is encouraging those troops to carry on that conduct. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the order of things, that's how it would appear. But in those situations, everybody had something of their own. Neither of my two commanders could have made me commit an atrocity. Everybody has within them a human side and a wild side. Anyone can become a murderer under certain circumstances, but I would not have permitted that. Maybe it's not for me to say this, but as far as I know our brigade commander, he was there briefly. But I think he is a person who would not have allowed this. You have to be born like that in order to do that. Maybe it's not for me to say, but I've taken the liberty of expressing my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But if your brigade commander disappointed you and, in fact, was aware that people --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
