utterances.text: Objection, objection, objection. There is no evidence that Mr. Blagojevic was there in Potocari during those days, that he witnessed or that he encouraged or that he participated --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm not suggesting that he was in Potocari. He didn't let me ask the question --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I totally object to this line of questioning, Your Honour. It's totally irrelevant; it has nothing to do with this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, there should be no arguments between the parties in front of the Judges at this stage. Mr. Karnavas, I believe that Mr. McCloskey is talking about a general situation, not particular in that location.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. President, he began by this hypothetical; I don't have a problem with that because I think that's in the evidence. But now when he starts saying Blagojevic disappointed him, based on his hypothetical, I can only assume that he's talking about Potocari. Now, if he's got proof, he should lay it out on the table and say: Here we have Blagojevic mistreating Muslims in front of his men, giving the green light to the men. Or here is Blagojevic that sees that his officers are mistreating Muslims, he's giving them a green light. Where is the evidence? We don't have any. So I do object to that line of questioning. I think it goes way too far and it's off-limits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I don't think so, Mr. Karnavas. I think this is the natural course of all the hypothetical questions that we have arrived at this point. But your objection is there and we will consider it. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And to clarify, Witness, I was not suggesting that Mr. Blagojevic was in Potocari. I'm asking generally if your commander disappointed you and in fact was aware that General Mladic or someone else had decided to kill hundreds and hundreds of prisoners. And his troops -- or that his officers knew that he knew this and he did nothing about it for several days, would that be a signal to his troops to carry that out, like you just said?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're leading me to a conclusion, but I can tell you that as far as I can recall and as far as I believe, the Bratunac Brigade was there, but it was to keep out of the way while others were doing their job. And probably Colonel Blagojevic kept as far away as he could from Mladic and those people. We could only have hindered them. We had to get out of the way, and that was the best thing to do. Mr. Blagojevic was not in charge. He could only have fared worse with Mladic. He was -- our people were nothing there. All we -- they had to do was keep out of the way. Whoever did -- whoever acted differently made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, you did not answer the question put to you by the Prosecution. It is a hypothetical question. You may repeat your question, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: My question is that: If your commander, at this time Blagojevic, was aware of a plan to murder thousands of people and his troops were involved in separating, guarding, transporting these people, and he never did anything to communicate to his troops that this was wrong, would that very fact that he didn't do anything and allowed his troops to work on this plan, would that be encouraging his troops to carry out the plan, just like the little hypothetical I gave you earlier? A commander that allows abuse to happen in front of him is signalling his men that it's okay.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already answered this question once. As far as it refers to me, a company commander, or the colonel of any other unit or any officer, if he does not draw his mens' attention to this, if he does not forbid them to do that, he is not acting well. If Mr. Blagojevic did this, it's not a good thing, but I abide by what I said. I believe that Mr. Blagojevic did not know what was going on. The only person who knew that - I didn't see him in Potocari - but it was Mr. Nikolic. He was perhaps the only person from our brigade who could decide whether certain things should be done. He had his own superior, but it was certainly not Mr. Blagojevic who issued orders to Nikolic. All the other people from our brigade knew little about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Going back to my question: Would an officer that did this, what you call a bad thing, would that be a signal to his troops that it was okay?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And that is just as applicable for a colonel in charge of a brigade as it is for a brigade commander in charge of a company?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is a fundamental principle of military command, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, I think you told us on direct that your battalion commander was -- you initially had told the OTP in your December 2001 interview that your battalion commander Zoran Jovanovic was present in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Reading this statement - I received it recently, it was promised earlier - I see that it's in there. As far as I can recall, however, I only said that the order I received came from Zoran, originated from Zoran, because he was the only one who could have issued it to me. And I said - and I abide by this now - that I received the order by courier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I'm not talking exactly about the order. I'm saying do you remember your interview in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Didn't you clearly tell the investigator that you saw your commander personally in Potocari on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps, I can't be sure, but a long time has elapsed, and now that I've seen the transcript of my interview in Banja Luka I see there are certain things in there that I think I said differently. And I may have made some mistakes, because one recalls things, things surface in the memory. I might recall other things in a year or two. But I'm sure now that I did not see Mr. Zoran Jovanovic in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I can read this back to you, but if I don't have to, I won't. Can you tell this Court: Did you or did you not tell us in Banja Luka that you saw your commander in Potocari? I'm talking about Zoran Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible that I said this in Banja Luka, but I think it was a misunderstanding. I am asserting now -- I know it says that here. I've seen it. I would like to hear the recording -- I'm not denying that I said that, but now having thought about it, I am sure I did not see him personally, that I received the order by courier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. So you acknowledge you clearly said that in Banja Luka. Now, did you have a chance to talk to Zoran Jovanovic after telling us that he was in Potocari on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean since then, to date? Or in Potocari? What time period are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I meant after speaking to us in Banja Luka and telling us that your -- you saw your commander in Potocari, did you happen to go see Jovanovic and tell him: By the way, I just spoke to the investigators and I told them the story and I told them you were in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We are friends. We see each other every day. We never discussed it. A person doesn't have to know everything. I talked to my neighbour who was the courier, and he reminded me that he had brought this order to me. A person sometimes forgets certain things.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, today you've testified that you stayed in Potocari for an hour or so and then you were told to go to an area a short distance from Potocari. I think you told the Prosecutor that was about 500 metres, something like that, in Banja Luka. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And now you've testified today that you and your unit stayed in that area about 500 metres from the Potocari gathering for the rest of the day on the 12th of July, all day the 13th of July, all day the 14th of July, and in the morning of the 15th of July you shipped out to Zvornik. Right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So what were you doing on the 12th after you left Potocari, the 13th, and the 14th with you and your men?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After we got back to the line, we stayed there the whole night. In the morning, as everything was already over, half the men went to have a rest; half remained, and I remained with them. The same happened the next day, and then we went to Zvornik. Because simply, we were the only unit on the left flank that stayed there; the others had moved on. We didn't have any tasks. The time before going to Zvornik was simply a time of rest for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So during those days, the 12th, the 13th, the 14th, you were just sitting around resting?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was so throughout the war, you just sat and waited. Half the unit, and the other half was home. So it was just sitting and waiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: People were doing a lot of work on the 12th and the 13th in Potocari, weren't they? There was a lot of soldiers working to secure that population and organise those buses and move those people out on those buses and take care of themselves, take care of people. There was a lot of work going on in Potocari 500 metres from where you guys were sitting around resting, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's not a big distance if you're on level ground, but this was all concealed from the view of the road. There were activities going on, but I don't know what was happening. Everybody had their own task to carry out, and I can't say anything about the tasks of other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And just to clarify, your map was a little unclear on the point of where you actually or where you were amongst the people. When you were in Potocari amongst the people, you were actually on that asphalt road between Bratunac and Srebrenica. Right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did go out amongst the people, but it's a rural area, or rather, Pecista was the place. And Potocari is the centre; it's on the asphalt road. But you have Potocari on both sides of the road, and Pecista is a village but following on from Potocari. So I went down the slope, down the mountain, to the village of Pecista on to the road. But as far as I am concerned, it's all Potocari to me. So not only on the asphalt road, but underneath Pecista and the route we traversed. There were people on that road all the time, in the courtyards, in the yards of houses, and all around.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I just want to make it clear that you were actually on that road amongst the people for a while, that asphalt road, that main road?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And while Potocari is a little village kind of off the road and Pecista is a little village off the road, this area where the Dutch compound was and where these factories were, that's what everybody just calls Potocari. Right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, where the DutchBat was, that is the entrance to Potocari. Actually, it's not Potocari proper. From that factory onwards, on the road, you have Potocari left and right, whereas Pecista is to the left and a little higher up from Potocari. But it's all Potocari, generally speaking, the factories themselves in Potocari and the road to Srebrenica for a kilometre and a half is Potocari, too. So it's a valley, and Potocari is on the left and on the right, villages both sides of the road, Budak, Gornji Potocari, all of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks. Thank you. I just wanted to clarify that. Did you have a chance to see the video of your interview, during your interview in Banja Luka? I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm just going to show this to you just briefly again and ask you a couple of questions. But let's start off with just a still shot if we could.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you see that okay?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, the person in sort of the brown T-shirt with a bit of a beard, is that a journalist? Is that the guy asking you questions?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. And he's holding a microphone, so it's a television reporter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Right. So there's a camera behind him. Okay. How about the guy behind you that we can see with the dark hair, the guy that's over your right shoulder, who's that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know the man.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: He's not from your unit?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. If he were from my unit, my soldier, I would know him. Even if he were from the battalion I would know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know Lieutenant Colonel Svetozar Kosoric? He's got some glasses --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So this guy over your left shoulder, we see him from his nose up. If you can take a look at it. We'll play the video and maybe we can freeze it when more of his face shows up.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can't see anything here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, just watch it. This is not a big thing. I just want you to watch this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, the one with the moustache and the bald one?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Right. He's Colonel Svetozar Kosoric --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never met the man.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you know that there was a chief of intelligence for the Drina Corps by that name?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's just play it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know any of those people on the screen?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Rade Micic, he's the one in the T-shirt. He was in the demining squad in our battalion, so the one in the black vest, Micic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How about the other guys? Do you know who they are?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We can see buses around. Were there a lot of buses around you at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see the bus now, but had somebody asked me whether there was a bus behind somewhere, I would have said no. So as you can see, I wasn't really aware of them. There were buses, I suppose, but I thought they were further away. Now I see that it's behind my back, and had you asked me yesterday, I would have said no, there wasn't a bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Why don't we keep playing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, when you gave that interview to the press, you knew it could be videoed, did you think you were doing anything wrong by being in Potocari at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't think about it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, do you remember what you told the Office of the Prosecutor about how long you stayed in the Bratunac area after Potocari?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say exactly. That would be going too far. Now, as we didn't know the time and time didn't mean much, we went -- well, let's take it in chronological order. I remember things that meant something. Now, all the rest of it along the way, the minor events, I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, do you recall telling the Office of the Prosecutor that you spent one night, the night of the 12th, in that location near Potocari, and the morning of the 13th you got on a bus and went to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I thought at the time, but having given it more thought later on -- well, that's why I say when we spoke and when I said "Zvornik," I didn't give dates because I emphasised that dates and days didn't mean anything to me. Because three years on, that period -- what are days for that entire period? You forget in the hope of getting through the days as quickly as possible. So it was just certain points in time, certain moments, assignments, things like that I remember; whereas, while you're lying down and are basically bored, you don't remember that. So I didn't agree, and I can't say now the 15th -- well, we just said that because there was the attack in Baljkovica, but otherwise -- and it's true, I was given an assignment, I went on assignment, and it was Zvornik between Potocari, the arrival at that line and all that, there was nothing in between.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You don't need to go into Baljkovica. I just wanted to confirm what you told us in Banja Luka. And when you spoke to us in Banja Luka and you said that you'd just spent one night there in Potocari and then left the next day, did you know at that time when you were talking to us in Banja Luka that a lot of bad things had allegedly happened the night of the 12th and on the day of the 13th in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't learn for a long time what happened, because I wasn't in the area for a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's a simple question. When you spoke to us that day and gave that answer about only spending one day in Potocari, did you at that time -- had you heard about all the alleged bad things that had happened on the 12th and the 13th in Potocari? It's a simple question.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't have any more questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any re-direct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I think I have a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: First of all, sir, I just want to clarify one point. When you said that you left Potocari on the 12th, where you took your new orders to position yourself, you said you were 500 metres away from Potocari. And I just want to be clear: Which way would you have gone, up towards the mountain, towards Bratunac, towards Srebrenica? Where were you located?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looking at it from Bratunac towards Srebrenica, it's the left-hand side, underneath the mountain. It's indicated on the map. It's the left-hand side or south, south-looking.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That would be where the woods are?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The edge of the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to show you a document that has come in; it's P490, if you could look at this. Now, do you recognise it, sir, or do you know what it is by looking at it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recognise this document. I've never had it -- I've never had the opportunity of seeing it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. If you look at the top, we see it's dated 15 July 1995. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the 15th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... that report. Right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And would this not be a daily combat report from the Bratunac Brigade to the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see at the bottom what it says. Now, whether it is the proper signature or not, I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. When you look at the top it says: "Daily combat report," and then it should say: "To command of the Drina Corps." Does it not state that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is beyond the scope. We're not challenging when he went to Zvornik either, if that's the misconception.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we haven't heard the question put by Defence counsel. But, Mr. Karnavas, I have to remind you that your questions should be within the scope of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank -- Your Honour, I can assure you, there's no need for you to remind me, but I do appreciate that. I can always use the guidance, but in this instance, in this instance, I assumed that there was some sort of an implication that the gentleman was fabricating, and I want to show him that there is a daily combat report here. And then my follow-up question was going to be whether he was aware that daily combat reports were being filed and sent off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think the witness has already answered that question. He's never seen this document. He doesn't know of the existence of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Which is understandable. Which is understandable.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may ask just two questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were you aware, sir, whether the Bratunac Brigade was sending daily command reports to the Drina Corps? Were you aware of that practice?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Then I won't ask any questions on that. How well do you know Colonel Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know him since his arrival in the brigade, or rather, mine and until now. But I think I have had the opportunity of getting to know him fairly well as a human being, as an individual.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you know him growing up?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sorry. I'm reminded just for the record that that video we showed was P89, for just -- so there's proper reference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, at this stage are there any documents to tender? Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, we do have just one document. That would be D142, the map that we displayed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. This document is admitted into the evidence. On the part of the Prosecution, are there any documents to tender?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. Well, Witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague to give your evidence. The usher will show you out of the room, and we wish you a pleasant journey back home. You may leave now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, are you ready for the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I am, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are there any protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: There are none.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I heard there is a change of the order of the witnesses according to your original list.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes. I became aware of that myself, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand the technical -- that there was a technical problem. I bear full responsibility for that, so it won't happen again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Can you -- since the next witness has no protective measures, could you please inform us about his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So that during the break we may find the right materials and the right people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes. Again, I apologise, Your Honours. His name is Radika Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just to clarify. If -- and if we need private session, that's fine. Who's after him and who's the next one, just so we can get ready for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Because I was a little confused on that, and proofing notes and exhibits are getting a little late, and I know what it's like to be in that position. But it would, of course, be helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, first of all, they haven't arrived yet. They're arriving shortly. We do have three, and I know that Mr. Zekic is going to be last. Of the other two, the names escape me right now and I have -- but if I could answer that question right after we come from the break so I can look at -- just to make sure in my mind. Because I'm also keeping in mind the time that we have, because I would like to get all three of them done by Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, that is a heavy workload.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I agree, but I was under the impression that I was being encouraged, shall we say, to move at a rapid clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. So you prefer that we have a break right now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yeah, for other reasons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: There are only 10 minutes left for this sitting. Yes, we'll resume at 20 past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, are you ready to tell us the order of the witness list for this week? If you need, we could go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. We -- the next person is Mr. Petrovic, Radika, who was the commander of the 4th Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade. Then we will have Zoran Cvjetinovic of the 2nd Company, 2nd Battalion. Then we have Mr. Mladin Vuksic, who was a simple soldier. And then we have Mr. Dragan Zekic, who was the commander of the 3rd Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade. And I was told that perhaps if necessary there was courtroom space available in the afternoons. I'm not suggesting, not suggesting, but I was told that there was availability of courtrooms. So we'll see how we get along with this fellow here, Mr. Petrovic, I expect two sessions, both for direct and cross, although I don't know what the Prosecution might want to do. The other two witnesses I suspect are going to be relatively short. Mr. Zekic, I would suspect to take about four sessions all together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And are they there?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: They are arriving today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You mean all of them?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All three of them are arriving today because the flight patterns -- well, the patterns haven't changed but the flight schedule has changed from Belgrade to Amsterdam. So we have fewer flights, and of course, there's some other logistical nightmares that keep popping up every day with new policies in the RS. But they're going to be arriving this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. As for the extra sitting, we'll look into the possibilities for that. And could we have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I guess it's good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what your name is.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: My name is Radika Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And could you please tell us your last name letter by letter.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: P-e-t-r-o-v-i-c.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. Could you please tell us where you're from.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I'm from Zelinje, Zvornik municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And could you please tell us a little bit about your educational background. Where did you go to school, how far did you go, what kind of schooling did you have.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I went to primary school in Drinjaca, the secondary vocational machine technology school in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And prior to the war, could you please tell us what your work experience was.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I worked for ten years in Partizanski Put , the Belgrade company, travelling around in the field. And after 1985, I moved to the company of Sperploca Jadar Zvornik and I worked there until the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what do you do today, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us again what you do today. Where are you working today, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I work in the republican administration for customs and tariffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And what is your position there? Do you have a title?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I am head of the customs department.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. If you could please tell us about your military experience or your background, did you do your military service with the JNA?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did do my military service for seven months in Tuzla -- or was it eight months? Anyway, afterwards I went to Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you attend any schooling while you were there?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In Tuzla, I completed the school for reserve officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you hold a rank prior to the commencement of the mobilisation process in 1992?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I was a captain by rank, reserve captain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So in the All People's Defence, that's what your rank was?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, in 1992, were you mobilised?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where you were mobilised.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I was mobilised to Zvornik on the 6th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, was that a brigade at the time or was that a TO, the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: It wasn't a brigade, it was the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And could you please tell us when you were mobilised what position, if any, did you hold?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I had the rank of komandir of the Zelinska Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us how large was this company.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: About 60 mobilised men.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, at some point we know that the Zvornik Brigade came into existence. Could you please tell us what you did from the time that you were mobilised until the time the Zvornik Brigade was formed.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: With the company, and they were the locals of the village of Zelinje, they would just belong to that company. We were in Zelinje, we would expect an attack, but the attack never came about. Nobody ever attacked us, until the end of the war. Zelinje was not attacked ever during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us what your location was.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: In Zelinje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, once the Zvornik Brigade was formed, what was your position then?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: All the companies who were there around Drinjaca belonged to the 2nd Battalion, the Drinjacki 2nd Battalion, the Zelinje, Ljesa [phoen], Djevanje [phoen] companies, and Drinjaca company.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And where did you -- in which battalion or company were you serving in?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I was the komandir of the Zelinje company, and the 2nd Infantry Battalion of the Zvornik Brigade. And its location was in Drinjaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, were those the same men that you had in your company that were serving with you when it was a Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, I want to fastforward to 1995, to July 1995 in particular. Could you please tell us what your position was at that point in time with the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: In July 1995 I found myself at the defence line of the Bratunac Brigade. I belonged to the Zvornik Brigade; however, we held the territory in the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So in other words your brigade was attached to the Bratunac Brigade, your battalion?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: If we can call the number of men I had a battalion, yes, we did perform work in the Bratunac Brigade. But we were in the rear towards the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, what battalion was this battalion when it was part of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: In Zvornik we were called the 8th Infantry Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And when you were attached to the Bratunac Brigade, what battalion did that become?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: We remained the 8th Zvornik Brigade, and the name of 4th Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade was added on to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, could you please tell us how many men were in this battalion.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: The battalion numbered 218 military recruits, conscripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And how many would be available to be on the lines at any given time?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: With the -- up at the line, there were never more than 80 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. How many companies were in or within the 4th Battalion?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Two companies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And so each company would have approximately 40. Is that -- would that be correct, serving at any given time on the line?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, roughly. Up at the defence line of the Bratunac Brigade and our duty was supply -- to supply men towards Pjenovac and we had responsibilities towards the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, when the 8th Battalion of the Bratunac -- of the Zvornik Brigade became attached to the Bratunac Brigade as the 4th Battalion, did it move its position?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Where did it move its position to?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: From Drinjaca we moved to the defence line at elevation 555 to the left, to elevation 561 at the right underneath Ravni Buljim.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us at what time, at what date, did the 8th Battalion of the Zvornik Brigade become attached to the Bratunac Brigade as the 4th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: The 22nd of September, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, from the 22nd of September, 1993, until July, say, 6th, 7th, 11th, 12th, 1995, did your lines change, your position, did it change?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if I could show you what has been marked for identification purposes as D138. You could look at this. Believe it or not, that's the only copy that we have, so you're going to have to work off that one. Could you please show us, and you'll have to, when you point, sir, you'll have to turn and point on the projector. If you could just show us where your line was located from September 22nd, 1993, until July 1995.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: It was by elevation 555 to elevation 651. 555, 651.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Hold it because we're trying to -- we may have to move it up a little bit. Where is 555? Could you point that out to us.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So -- okay. Now, from 555, where was your line located?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: The line was located going from 555 to 651.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now -- and both companies would be from -- between those two points?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The first company held the line from feature 651, eight trenches moving towards feature 555. And then 1 kilometre was not covered, going through a creek and meadow. And the second one was from 555, seven trenches.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So -- and between the 1st and the 2nd Company, there was a kilometre, I understand it, that was not covered?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, in each trench, how many soldiers were in there?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: At the most, five soldiers in each.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How many trenches were in the 1st Company?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: The 1st Company had eight trenches.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And how many trenches did the 2nd Company have?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: The 2nd Company had seven trenches.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where your command post was located.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And does it have a name? Does that location that's slightly north, north-east, of 555, does it have a name?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: It was in Kajici, 1 and a half to 2 kilometres away from the asphalt road moving towards feature 555.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, if we look on this map, sir, and we look further up north, slightly north-west, we see Kajici there, do we not?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And you've indicated that further down, sort of south, south-east, is where your headquarters were located. And you also indicated that that area was called Kajici.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: At the beginning when we arrived, the command post was at Kajici by the asphalt road. In the first half of 1994, pursuant to orders from the brigade commander, Pandurevic, I had to relocate towards the line. At his request, this was supposed to be exactly between the 1st and 2nd Company in the interim space there, because as there was no building there or any facility we could put up in, I located 2 to 3 kilometres from asphalt in the last house towards the line on the right-hand side. It was a burnt-down house. We renovated it a bit, and that's where we were accommodated. And the kitchen remained asphalt because we didn't have any water. So there were two cooks down there and stablemen taking food up to the line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, first of all if I could get you to mark on the map itself where the headquarters would be. We're going to give you a pen, I want you to -- so we can have a -- if you can just write on it.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. That's a circle. Do you want to put IKM? Is that how you would reflect it to be the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: That was the forward command -- that was the command. There was no forward command post, because I was there all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, where were the cooks? You indicated that there were a couple of cooks and that they would cook the food and bring it up to the line.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And so for the record this -- the gentleman marked it with a dot further up north, right by Kajici. All right. Now, what was the distance between where those cooks were located and your headquarters?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: 3 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And how would you get there?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: We had a van.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And the van would take you all the way from the road where the cooks were all the way to your headquarters?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, what kind of means of communications did you have?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: With Bratunac and Zvornik, we had a telephone line. Cables laid down beside the asphalt road to Bratunac, and then from Bratunac on there was a telephone line to Zvornik. We did not have radio communications, either with Bratunac or with Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So you didn't have a Motorola?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How far were you from the Bratunac Brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: About 12 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And how far were you from the Zvornik Brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: About 35 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, once you became attached to the Bratunac Brigade, who assigned the men, you know, their rotation? How many would come up, when and so forth?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: It was assigned by the command of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And who would provide the materiel assistance necessary for you and your men to function up there, be it food, clothing, transportation?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: We received all this from the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did the Bratunac Brigade provide anything?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: To your understanding, keeping in mind that you were now the 4th Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade, who was your commander?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I respected both commanders, the commander of the Bratunac Brigade and the commander of the Zvornik Brigade. I carried out the orders of both, as far as I was able to. But I was oriented more toward the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: During that period of time from September 22nd, 1993, to July 1995, while you were attached to the Bratunac Brigade did you receive orders from the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When receiving orders from the Zvornik Brigade, did you inform the commander of the Bratunac Brigade that, one, you had received an order; and two, whether permission was being granted from the Bratunac Brigade for you to carry out those orders from the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No, no. I did not pass on information, nor did I ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, didn't you think it was necessary, since now you were no longer the 8th Battalion but rather -- of the Zvornik Brigade, but rather the 4th of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I was simultaneously a member of the 4th Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade and a member of the 8th Battalion of the Zvornik Brigade. I was duty-bound to carry out the tasks given to me by both of these brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us into what point of time in history did you go back to the Zvornik Brigade? In other words, leave the Bratunac Brigade as a 4th Battalion and go back to the Zvornik Brigade as the 8th Battalion?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: On the 19th of July, 1995, in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And pursuant to whose orders did you go back to the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Pursuant to orders from the commander of the Zvornik Brigade, Colonel Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if I could show you a document. Now, could you just look at that, sir. This would appear, would it not, to be a daily combat report dated 19 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I've read the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And for the record this would be D135 for identification. Now, at the top we see it's a daily combat report from the Bratunac Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And if we go into paragraph 2 at the last sentence, and I'll read it. Perhaps you can follow along. It says: "We do not know by whose order the 4th Battalion was attached to the 1st Zvornik Light Infantry Brigade." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And as far as you know, this was the date that you returned by order from Pandurevic to go back to the Zvornik Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And from reading this report, this combat daily report, it would appear that the Bratunac Brigade was not even informed by the Zvornik Brigade or by Pandurevic that your battalion now was going back from Bratunac to the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, could you please tell us briefly if you can recollect any instances where you received orders from the Zvornik Brigade, what sort of orders did you receive during that period of time, that is from 1993, September 22nd, to July 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: In this period I was constantly sending about 20 men to Pjenovac, 20 were on leave, 20 were at Pjenovac, that is, and 20 were at home resting after having returned from Pjenovac. So that I always had 60 men at my line in Kajici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, just as a way of example, I want to show you a document --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just by way of example, I want to show you a document which regrettably we have yet to have translated, but perhaps you can read this one line, look at it. And for identification purposes it will be D140. And I marked the appropriate portion that I want you to focus on. But if you could look at this document first and please tell us what the document is.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: This shows that a brigade was to be formed, which was to be located in the area of Zvornik. I received an order that in Konjevic Polje, Drinjaca, Sopotnik, and Kruske, I should prepare certain buildings to accommodate these soldiers. I received the order from the commander of the Zvornik Brigade, and with another officer I carried out this task.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, with all due respect to speeding up the proceedings, it's very difficult to follow the witness when we don't have an English translation, at least of the key parts. I think this should have been necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we also --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour. I totally agree. I found it this morning, and I had hoped that it would -- the key part would have been translated by this point in time. But as I indicated before I commenced that it hadn't been. I just wanted to get that one bit of information from the gentleman and the date and then -- before tendering it. We will have that portion translated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please, by looking at this document, tell us when you were ordered by the Zvornik Brigade to undertake those tasks that you just told us, just by looking at the document.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I received it in early 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, could you -- it has a date. The document does have a date, does it not, sir, if you could look at the document.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. The 19th of January, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And is it the 19th or the 15th? Perhaps if you could look at the document, physically look at the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If Madam Usher could hand the gentleman the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you could look at the document and look at the top.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's the 15th of January, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And if you look at the next page, whose signature is on this document?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: It is the signature of the commander of the Zvornik Brigade, Vinko Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And if I understand your testimony correctly thus far, during this period of time you had already been attached to the Bratunac Brigade as the 4th Battalion. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall whether you carried out this task?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you recall whether on this particular occasion, in light of the task that was involved, whether you contacted the Bratunac Brigade, the commander of the Bratunac Brigade, to get permission to go to that area and carry out the tasks that were being asked of you by, I believe it was a major, Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to focus your attention to July 1995. And as a point of reference, if we take the 11th of July, 1995, as the day that Srebrenica fell, I think it's pretty well-established in this court that the attack on Srebrenica began on the 6th of July, 1995. So could you please tell us when you became aware that there was going to be an attack on Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't aware there was going to be an attack on Srebrenica. It was only when I learned it had been attacked that I became aware of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you recall whether prior to the attack, prior to the 6th, you had attended any meetings at the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you tell us what date that was.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: It was the 3rd of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us who was at this meeting.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: The commander of the Bratunac Brigade, Blagojevic; I think the operations man, Eskic; all the battalion commanders, together with me, four of us; then there was the security man, Momir Nikolic; and several other members of the Bratunac Brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, could you please tell us what was the nature of the meeting, what was discussed.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: At this meeting, the commander informed us of the fact that in Srebrenica there was a large number of armed men, that there was a possibility of their attacking our lines and attempting to break through towards Tuzla. He assigned tasks to the battalions, and he assigned a task to my battalion, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, do you recall what assignment you had received?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: My task was to hold our line of defence firmly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, isn't that what you had been doing for the last couple of years, holding that line?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: From 1993 to 1995, July, had you been given any orders, either by the Zvornik Brigade or the Bratunac Brigade, to advance, to try to gain any territory?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you said that that was the 3rd of July, 1995. Now, I want to show you what has been marked as P406 as an exhibit. If you could look at it, please. If you could tell us whether you recognise the document.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But do you know what the document is if you look at the first page?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if I could focus your attention on paragraph 5.4. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, could you take a moment and read it, read it to yourself, because I will ask you some questions about that particular paragraph.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, it states here - I'm going to go slowly, step by step - that: "The 4th Battalion will carry out decisive defence of current combat positions." What did you understand -- what do you understand that to be?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: In my view, decisive defence means we must firmly hold the positions we are at.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Behind you, incidentally, behind those trenches, was there a second or a third echelon of forces that would protect your rear in the event the Muslim forces broke through those trenches, that line of defence that you had been holding for some three years?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No. There was only a line of trenches.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Behind, there was free territory, people lived there. There was even a civilian police station in Kravica, there was civilian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. It then goes on to say: "With its own BVG, battalion fire support group, it prevent movement and regrouping of the enemy forces primarily in the Jaglici, Lupoglav, and Gradina sectors." Do you recall whether you as commander of the 4th Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade carried out this task?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: We were constantly monitoring the territory in front of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if I could -- if you could be so kind as to look at the map that I handed you earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And for the record, it's 138.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And if we could put it on the ELMO, because it's unfortunately the only copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: By that, I meant the only copy that we have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. If you could look at the map, sir, and could you please tell us what area are you being asked, with your battalion fire support group, to prevent movement and regrouping, the Jaglici, Lupoglav, and Gradina sectors. Could you please show that to us on the map.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You might want to use the pointer, it's a little easier.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Lupoglav, Jaglici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And do you see Gradina? Maybe it's not on that part of the map I've given you. In any event, from looking at that location, at least the one part that you were able to find, how far is that location from where your 1st Company would have been located - and as I understand it, that's on point 651 that we see on the map - what's the distance?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: The distance is about a kilometre and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. During that period of time on the attack of Srebrenica, did you carry out this? Did you use your battalion fire support to prevent any movement in that area?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I didn't -- I don't have any heavy weapons. There were only infantry weapons at the line. And there was no need, because there was no grouping. At Jaglici, there was an UNPROFOR observation post, and the Muslims didn't dare come out here because of them probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So this task was not carried out because there was no need to, if I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: That's right. There was no need for me to take any action.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Then it goes on and it says: "It should pay special attention to its right flank." Who is on your right flank?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: At my right flank, there was the Milici battalion for a time. Then they withdrew and left and set up a line from Brezinci to Ravni Buljim and Kosar. The space in between from elevation 651 to Brezinci remained empty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: From 651 and Brezinci is 631, that area was uncovered?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. After they left it, the area remained uncovered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And then it says: "It will support the brigade artillery group from its current positions according to the plan and requests." Did you by any chance during that period of time, the attack on Srebrenica, from the 6th of July, 1995, to the 11th of July, 1995, did you provide any support to the brigade artillery group from your current positions?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: It was the other way around. The brigade fire group was supposed to provide me with support if I needed it, but I didn't need it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And then it says that: "The IKM, the TT651 sector." What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: This means the forward command post. My command post should be in the 1st Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, do you -- did you recall whether that was where your command post was during those days?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I often toured the lines, and I was often in both of the companies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us, since you are the 4th Battalion, if my memory serves me correctly, right after you comes the 1st Battalion and then the 2nd and then the 3rd. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So what if your neighbours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Well, he's certainly leading this question. There has been quite a considerable number of leading questions. I don't understand or then see whether this witness testified before that there were other companies -- other battalions. He talked about his companies, but not about other battalions. And just for correction purposes, the witness said before a "Milici Battalion." And I'm not sure whether he said it or whether it was wrongly interpreted, I believe there is a Milici Brigade but not a battalion, which was at the right side of his lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe Mr. Karnavas could help us with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: First of all, let's deal with Milici. Is it a battalion or a brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: The Milici Battalion was next to us, and it was within the composition of the Milici Brigade, which I assume had a number of battalions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Do you know how many battalions were in the Milici Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the Bratunac Brigade, help us out here, it's been some time. How many battalions did the Bratunac Brigade have?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: The Bratunac Brigade had three battalions, and I was the 4th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Was there a 5th or a 6th or a 7th by any chance?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, would you please tell us who was your neighbour with respect to the Bratunac Brigade. You have Milici on one side. Who is your next neighbor?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: To my right was the Milici Battalion. And on the left, the 1st Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And after the 1st Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade, what followed?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: The 2nd and then the 3rd, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So it was the 4th, the 1st, the 2nd, and the 3rd?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How close was your neighbour, that is, from the Bratunac Brigade, the 1st Battalion?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: The first trench, their first trench, was about 100 metres from where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And so for 100 metres, there is this gap?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's customary. There's always about 100 metres' space between trenches, and that's what it was like with my trenches, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, to your knowledge, from the 6th to the 11th, what combat activities was the 4th Battalion engaged in?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: The 4th Battalion was engaged in its regular tasks of defence at their lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I'm -- but with respect to the attack and the fall of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No. We had no responsibilities like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you advance at all?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: From the 22nd of September, 1993, up until the 19th of July, 1995, we were in the same trenches. We didn't advance anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you have any Muslim forces that were nearby you that you could see and shoot at during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you ever shoot at any Muslim forces or Muslim men that were perhaps going in that area towards Tuzla? And I'm referring to the period from the 6th to the 11th.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No, no. We didn't even see them. We didn't see them moving about at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: From the 6th to the 11th, were you ever paid any visits by any higher echelon officers, and I'll start with General Mladic. Did he come by?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No. No officers visited our side, from the corps or from the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So I take it that even the commander of the Bratunac Brigade, Mr. Blagojevic, he didn't come over?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No. Commander Blagojevic only came by when he took over his duty. And when he left, he didn't come again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you indicated to us that you had a means of communication by way of a line that would connect you to the Bratunac Brigade headquarters and the Zvornik Brigade headquarters. During that period of time, the 6th through the 11th, do you recall whether you contacted either the Bratunac Brigade or the Zvornik Brigade to get any instructions or to check in or for any other reasons?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No, there was no need.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall whether you received any orders by way of courier, somebody coming and hand-delivering you an order, either from the Bratunac Brigade or the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did anyone keep you abreast, keep you informed, as to how things were going on with respect to the attack on Srebrenica so at least you would know how the VRS forces were doing?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No, nobody kept us informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you during this period of time, from the 6th to the 11th, leave your position and go, say, to Zvornik or home or anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I don't think I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you think whether you -- well, do you know or think that during those days you might have visited the Bratunac Brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, could you please tell us to the best of your recollection when was it that you first learned that Srebrenica had fallen?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: On the 11th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall what time of day it was?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: In the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you learned of this, were you given any specific instructions?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you recall how you learned it and from whom?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I learned it from people who would come to the line, from home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, now that Srebrenica had fallen, did you by any chance leave the line?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did any of your men leave the line, if you know, during that period? And we're talking about the 12th now -- I'm sorry, the 11th.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did anything, anything, unusual happen on the 11th of July, 1995, the day that Srebrenica fell?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So now I'm going to move on to the next day, the day after Srebrenica fell, that would be 12 July 1995. Could you please tell us where you were on that day, in the morning.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: In the morning, I was at the command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And now was your command post where it had always been or was it still or had it been moved to the point 651 as a forward command post?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No. It was where it always was, about 1 and a half to 2 kilometres away from the asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So what happened on that day? What do you recall?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: In the morning between 6.00 and 7.00, the komandir of the 1st Company informed the command that up the hill at Jaglici he noticed a large group of Muslims of between 100 to 200 people. And I informed the chief of the Zvornik Brigade by phone, and the duty operations officer in Bratunac of the Bratunac Brigade. I think at the time it was Eskic. I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: And after having informed the Zvornik and Bratunac Brigade, I went to the 1st Company so I could be at the forward command post there and see for myself and to be together with my men.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, let me stop you here. If you recall - and I know it's been many years - but if you recall, which brigade did you call first, the Bratunac or the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: The Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And could you tell us why you would contact the Zvornik Brigade first when, in fact, by this point in time, at least on paper, you are attached to the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I considered myself to be a member of the Zvornik Brigade always, and whatever I needed they would do for me. I didn't ask the Bratunac Brigade for anything, nor did they do anything for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you contacted the Zvornik Brigade, did you receive any particular instructions or orders?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not receive any instructions, but I asked that people be found to close off the space in between on my right, because I was under threat with so few men and such a large number of Muslims who had advanced towards my positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, let me make sure I understand the sequencing. You heard -- you hear about this group of 100 or 200 Muslims from the komandir of the 1st Company that's on point 651 on the map. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: At that point in time, you're at your headquarters. Right? You're going to have to answer so we can get it on the record.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, how did you learn of this if you did not have a radio? How was this communicated to you?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: It was communicated through -- by the phone. We had a field telephone from the command to both companies, an inductor telephone of the military type.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us whether it was you personally who contacted the Zvornik Brigade, or was it someone else, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I personally contacted them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Can you recall with whom did you speak in the Bratunac Brigade -- I mean in the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I talked to Major Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So you personally spoke to him, not the duty officer?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I spoke to him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And that's when you conveyed the information that you had, and I believe you indicated you asked for some reinforcements. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I asked that men be found and that somebody be asked to close off the area to the right of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, to the right of you again, could you please remind us of what's there.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: To the right of me before was in Milici Battalion, and they had withdrawn and left that position, so the space remained uncovered, empty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And what was the length of that uncovered space, that no-man's-land, if we can call it that?
