utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: By road, about 3 and a half kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And do you recall how many men did you request as reinforcements for that distance?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I didn't ask for any specific number, because it wasn't my line. But just for the security of the men, I asked that this area be closed off or covered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall what his response was?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: He said he's do his best.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did -- and I take it after that is when you called the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, when you called the Bratunac Brigade, did you inform them that there was in gap of some 3 kilometres to your right and that in light of the situation you would need some reinforcements?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas is leading again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's not a leading question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: He's testifying the whole morning. This time it's really relevant. I mean, earlier, he said about the cooks cooking the meals on the lines, bringing it to the front lines, but I think now it's getting to serious issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you have to put your question another way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you call the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What did you say to them?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I informed them that at Jaglici the Muslims were grouping and that the group numbered 100 to 200 men, and that they were moving, advancing, towards my positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you inform them that you had called the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you inform them that you had a need for men?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you inform them that you had spoken with Major Obrenovic?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us why you did not inform them of this conversation that you had with the Bratunac -- with the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I didn't ask them for reinforcements, because had they had the men they wouldn't have asked the Zvornik Brigade for us to arrive there. And I never conveyed to them what I conveyed to Zvornik or vice versa. I didn't tell Zvornik what I told them; I didn't feel the need to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you ever contact the Bratunac Brigade prior to this period seeking men or reinforcements?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you told us that you had this conversation with Mr. Obrenovic, and you told us that he said that he would do something about it. Did men ever arrive?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us when did they arrive.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: They arrived on the 12th, or rather, during the night between the 12th and 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us how many men arrived.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: 40 men arrived. I think they were from Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you said from Vlasenica, so could you please tell us, if you know, from what brigade they were from.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did they come with any instructions?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us what those instructions were.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: When they arrived, they took up their positions straight away from feature 651 towards Siljkovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did they have instructions before they arrived or did they receive instructions when they arrived?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I don't know who gave them those instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know whether they were subordinated to you or whether they were there working alongside of you?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: They were not subordinated to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you have any contact with these men during that period?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know who was their komandir?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I think it was Gagic or Garic, a surname like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, on the 12th did anything else happened that you learned that there were these men of 100 or 200 and after you had placed the calls, the telephone calls, to the Zvornik Brigade and the Bratunac Brigade, did anything else happen?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please describe to us what happened.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: After my conversation with Zvornik and Bratunac, I left to go to the 1st Company at feature 651. I withdrew two of the last trenches on the right-hand side. I withdrew the men so that I could defend my flank. And that is how those trenches remained until the new group arrived on the morning of the 13th, when I returned the two trenches to the trenches they were in initially. As in the 1st Company, the men were under threat and we expected to see a breakthrough, either at us or by us. We expected a large number of Muslims to go by. I went to the 2nd Company to talk to the people there from the 2nd Company and to see whether they would leave two men per trench and allow the other men to go and fill in the trenches to make the people there more certain. I stayed there until evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: And the men accepted my explanations and acted upon it, and they went to the 1st Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: In the meantime, while I was in the 2nd Company, the 1st Company took one Muslim prisoner; they captured him. And they informed the command or signalsmen in the command that they had a captured Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me stop you here. I want to go step by step. First of all, do you recall what time on the 12th was it that you visited the 1st Company that was at point 651?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi --

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I don't think he said he visited the 1st Company. He said while he was at the 2nd Company. The 1st Company --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I understand the gentleman wishes to be obstructionistic today, but if he can look at the monitor, it says: "After my conversation with the Zvornik and Bratunac, I left to go to the 1st Company at feature 651." I read it verbatim from here, hoping to draw an objection, hoping to show how obstructionistic he's being today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And he bought the bait, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So we were saying: About what time did you go to the 1st Company that's located at 651?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I went to the 1st Company at point 651. I went there at around 7.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I stayed there until 1.00, 1300 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, from your command post to the 1st Company, how long would it take you to get there?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: About one hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And how would you get there?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: You can only go on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were you by yourself or were there others with you?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't alone. There were two other soldiers with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, after you left the 1st Company, you indicated you went to visit the 2nd Company. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How long did it take you to go to where the 2nd Company was located?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And how did you get there?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I walked. That's the only way you can get there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was anyone with you?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the two soldiers that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I believe you indicated that some time -- that when you arrived at the 2nd Company you received some information about a prisoner. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Then please tell us exactly what -- when was it that you learned about this prisoner.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I learned about the prisoner when I returned to the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And when did you return to the command?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: In the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: About what time?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you recall who was it that gave you this information?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: The signalsman, Milos Savic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, if you recall, what information you learned on the evening hours at around 7.00, and this would be the 12th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I received information that the 1st Company had a captured Muslim and that the chief of the Zvornik Brigade had been informed of that, Obrenovic, and that he had issued orders that the prisoner be taken to Kajici, to the asphalt road there, in order to be taken over by Vukotic, a security man in the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, let me stop you here. Do you recall learning about what time it would have been when the 1st Company had come across this Muslim? When did they capture him?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: The 1st Company didn't come across him; he came across the 1st Company. Because the company was stationary, whereas he went by their positions and surrendered, gave himself up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know whether this individual was armed? Did you learn whether he had been armed or unarmed?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you recall about what time of day when this Muslim surrendered himself to the 1st Company?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But you do recall, as I understand your testimony correctly, that you would have left the 1st Company sometime around 1.00. That's your recollection?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and at that time there was no prisoner.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you said that they told you that the 1st Company had contacted Mr. Obrenovic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: The 1st Company reported to the signalsmen at the command, because they couldn't have gotten a connection to Obrenovic. And from the signalsmen, Major Obrenovic was informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And this is what you learned?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, where exactly -- and what exactly did they tell you as far as Obrenovic's instructions were?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: They said that it had been ordered that the prisoners should be taken down to the asphalt road at Kajici, and that Vukotic would come and collect him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, from the 1st Company to Kajici, where they would take him by the road, would the -- any members of the 1st Company, would they have to travel by the 2nd Company in order to get to the road at Kajici?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And as I understand it, you learned that Obrenovic had sent somebody up there that would pick up this prisoner?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what is his name again?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Dusko Vukotic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you know this gentleman?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you know his position?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And could you please tell us, to your understanding, what was his position within the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: He worked in security.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, aside from learning that information, did you learn whether the prisoner had been turned over to Mr. Vukotic?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I learned that he had not been turned over.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Did you learn what had happened to him?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And one final question and we'll pick it up from here tomorrow, but if you could just briefly tell us: What did you learn about this prisoner? What happened to him?

utterances.speaker: RADIKA PETROVIC
utterances.text: After Obrenovic's order that the prisoner be taken along the asphalt road to Kajici, the komandir of the 1st Company designated soldiers to escort him to Kajici. The road that had to be taken is close to a minefield. According to what the komandir of the company said, they took the prisoner, and he started trying to escape. He went toward the minefield which had trip-wire mines. Their lives would have been all in danger, because he would have activated the mines, and they would have all have been killed. That's why they shot the prisoner and killed him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, sir. We're going to pick up from here tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, as for the extra sitting time, we have been informed that the only time available is tomorrow afternoon. We might have an extra sitting tomorrow afternoon from 3.00 to 4.30, 90 minutes, but we will continue tomorrow morning in this courtroom. And tomorrow afternoon -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If I could just take 10 seconds and announce that I've informally tried to tell many of the people, but the -- we have decided not to appeal the Rule 98 bis decision of the Court, but we will be filing a motion to amend the indictment, consistent with recent case law. And I wanted to be able to -- so my B/C/S colleagues would understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you for your information. Well, Witness, thank you very much for giving your evidence this morning. I'm afraid that you have to stay in The Hague for another day because we haven't finished your testimony. So during your stay here, do not talk to anybody and do not let anybody talk to you about your testimony. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We will resume at 9.00 tomorrow morning in the same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: at 1.50 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday, the 6th day of May, 2004, at 9.00 a.m. 25
